discoveries.summary: Recent work shows that large language models (LLMs) can operate directly on the parameters of other neural networks. They can read what a network was trained to do, fix a network that fails, and write working networks from scratch, all without gradient descent. This capability has been termed Weight-Space Programming (WSP). Exploring this new paradigm systematically requires a robust benchmark. discoveries.summary: AI judges, models that grade another system's output against a rubric, extend clinical review to the scale at which clinical AI writes.
